observation: In run r3 a blindspot-review returned changes_required after the review-round limit, raising a review_changes_required Attention. The fix was made in the workspace after the last build submission. Resolving the Attention resumed blindspot-review (not build); after its pass, verify refused with CANDIDATE_MISMATCH because the governed candidate was the earlier build tree. Submitting verify as failed raised a runner_failed Attention whose resolution would re-run verify against the same stale candidate. Separately, build submission refused with STALE_CANDIDATE once the work was committed, because the workspace HEAD must equal the governed base commit.

evidence.summary: agent-loop pipeline run returned CANDIDATE_MISMATCH (workspace tree f08c299b vs governed de79fc5c) after Attention attention:bd1aa30218239c6f resumed blindspot-review attempt 3; verify failed raised attention:7f5c9325f919886e; build submit after commit 74e3ad60 returned STALE_CANDIDATE (HEAD 74e3ad60 vs base f85fffed). Recovered via Contract revision 4 and a detached worktree at f85fffed.

hypothesis: Attention resolution resumes the interrupted stage with attempt+1 and has no route back to build, so any candidate change after the last build cannot enter the governed candidate without a new Run.
validated_conclusion: When a fix is needed after review rounds are exhausted, resolving the review Attention cannot carry the new candidate; recovery requires superseding the Contract to start a fresh Run, and build/verify must be submitted from a workspace whose HEAD is the governed base (e.g. a detached worktree with the diff applied uncommitted).
